solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hack holds page displaying a prominent headline

indicators.note: holds says the first word keeps another piece within its letters

parts.note: to hack is to slash

explanation.surface: A journalist shows off a big headline he has written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a journalist, fitting the newspaper picture, but here it is the verb meaning to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: In newspaper jargon a splash is the main front-page story with its large banner headline.

clue.text: Quietly departed with item of crockery

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
the late are those who have departed this life

explanation.surface: Someone slips away silently carrying a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate is a flat dish, a basic piece of crockery on any dinner table.

clue.text: Former name of country with bottomless pit in one area

parts.note: an abyss is a seemingly bottomless chasm
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A geography question about an old country containing a deep chasm somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container signal here; its own two letters go into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia was the older Western name for Ethiopia, used until the mid-twentieth century.

clue.text: Hired assassin in bestseller by soldier

parts.note: a bestseller is a hit
man is used for a private soldier, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A contract killer appears in a popular thriller alongside a military man.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitman is a criminal paid to murder someone, a professional killer for hire.

clue.text: Film celebrities eating with a king

indicators.note: eating says the first word takes the following pieces inside it

parts.note: famous people are stars
R is Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Movie celebrities dine alongside a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Wars is the famous space-opera movie franchise begun by George Lucas in 1977.

clue.text: Soporific drug helps eating disorder

indicators.note: disorder says the letters of the preceding words are put into a muddled arrangement

explanation.surface: A sleeping pill is said to help someone with an eating disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating disorder' reads as one medical term, but 'eating' is fodder and 'disorder' the anagram signal; 'drug' is fodder too, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A soporific, used as a noun, is a substance that induces sleep, such as a sedative potion.

clue.text: Star taking chance after collapse of seat

indicators.note: after puts the risk piece behind the rearranged letters
a collapse wrecks the structure of the word seat, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to take a chance is to risk something

explanation.surface: A celebrity gambles after their chair gives way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapse of' gives ASTE; 'Star' is the printed symbol, not a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the small star-shaped symbol used in printing to mark a footnote.

clue.text: Talk about learner driver a good deal

indicators.note: about says the first word goes round the next piece

parts.note: to have a word is to talk
L is the learner plate shown by a British learner driver

explanation.surface: A conversation about a novice motorist getting a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a good deal' looks like a bargain but means a great amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A world of something, as in a world of difference, means a huge amount of it.

clue.text: High-quality car on left turns on its side?

parts.note: Rolls, short for Rolls-Royce, is the byword for a luxury car
something left is over, as in left over

explanation.surface: A luxury car topples onto its side on the left-hand bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing one piece by the other; the question mark admits a vehicle that rolls over does more than lie on its side.
explanation.definitionFit: To roll over is to turn from lying one way onto one's side or back.

clue.text: Financial security obtained by a setter? Yes, surprisingly!

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that the letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is delighted to have earned a comfortable living.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of A SETTER YES is signalled by 'surprisingly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on easy street is an idiom for living in comfortable affluence, free of money worries.

clue.text: Regret bringing in Liberal government

indicators.note: bringing in says the first word takes the next piece inside

parts.note: to rue is to regret
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in British politics

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry about electing a Liberal administration.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule is government or control, as in a period of direct rule.

clue.text: Reportedly outstanding on distinct musical instrument

indicators.note: reportedly says a word is used only for how it is pronounced

parts.note: a debt outstanding is due
a sharp image is distinct and clear

explanation.surface: A news item that a distinctive instrument has been played superbly.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech due is often said like 'jew'; 'on' is a link placing one piece before the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jew's harp is a small metal frame with a twanging tongue, held against the mouth and plucked.

clue.text: Salad vegetable in a meal linked to recipe

parts.note: R is the old abbreviation for recipe, from Latin take
a dish is a meal or course

explanation.surface: Instructions for a dish that features a crunchy salad root.
explanation.definitionFit: The radish is a peppery red root eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Sign in some newcomers

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Some new arrivals are seen as a portent.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'some' into 'newcomers'.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign of what is to come, a portent good or bad.

clue.text: Cocktail — a small measure knocked over by girl

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up the other way, so the words a and gram are read backwards

parts.note: a gram is a small unit of weight
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman tips over someone's little tot of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' gives MARGA; 'small measure' suggests a tot of spirits, but it is a unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A margarita is a tequila cocktail with lime and orange liqueur, served in a salt-rimmed glass.

clue.text: A sudden drop, so I need changes involving volts

indicators.note: involving says the rearranged letters take another piece inside them
changes says the letters of so I need are rearranged

parts.note: V is the symbol for volts

explanation.surface: An electrician notes a sudden power dip and needs to alter the voltage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' gives NOSEDIE, and 'involving' wraps it round the volts symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosedive is a steep plunge, by an aircraft or by prices, so a sharp fall.

clue.text: Depressed? Less than in Perth, possibly

parts.note: feeling down is feeling depressed
under means less than, as in under ten

explanation.surface: Someone feeling low wonders whether things are worse in Perth.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth here is the Western Australian city, not the Scottish one; 'possibly' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Down Under is the informal term for Australia and New Zealand, where Perth lies.

clue.text: Photograph fracture and crack

parts.note: to snap is to break or fracture
to have a crack at something is to have a shot

explanation.surface: An X-ray image shows a broken bone and a crack.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quickly taken informal photograph.

clue.text: Made a minister end radio broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering, so the letters of end and radio are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman's appointment brings a radio programme to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ordained is to be formally made a priest or minister of the church.

clue.text: Pull back, making room

indicators.note: back says the word for pull is read in the other direction

parts.note: to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: Someone retreats to make space.
explanation.definitionFit: A ward is a room in a hospital where patients are cared for.

clue.text: False rumour an eccentric put about

indicators.note: put about says the first word is placed round the next

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: An oddball spreads an untrue story.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is an unfounded report or hoax, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Be suspended at college, causing an emotional problem

parts.note: to hang is to be suspended
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student is sent down, which leaves them troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspended' suggests a student punished by the college, but here it simply means dangling.
explanation.definitionFit: A hang-up is a neurosis or emotional inhibition someone cannot shake off.

clue.text: Confined to school, some cheating at Edinburgh

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pupil kept in after being caught copying at an Edinburgh school.
explanation.definitionFit: A gated pupil is confined to school grounds as a punishment, a British boarding-school term.

clue.text: Fizzy cola — a cup drunk inside a bay on the Pacific

indicators.note: inside says the second jumble sits within the first
fizzy suggests bubbling up, so the letters of cola are stirred about
drunk suggests unsteadiness, so the letters of a cup are jumbled

explanation.surface: A soft drink is gulped from a cup at a Pacific resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fizzy' gives ALCO and 'drunk' gives CAPU, the second going 'inside' the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is the Mexican resort city on a large bay of the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Swear remedy involves sun

indicators.note: involves says the first word wraps round another piece

parts.note: a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: A treatment for sunburn makes someone use bad language.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to swear, to utter oaths or profanity.

clue.text: Head of faculty coming in to pose riddle

indicators.note: coming in says that letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the word faculty

explanation.surface: The faculty head arrives to set students a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddle' looks like a puzzle but is the verb meaning to pass through a sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: To riddle soil or grain is to sift it through a coarse sieve.

clue.text: Stranded dinghy had broken down crossing river

indicators.note: crossing says the reassembled letters span another piece placed within
broken down says the letters of dinghy and had are split up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A small boat broke down while crossing the water, leaving its crew marooned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken down' makes HIGHANDDY, and 'crossing' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Left high and dry means stranded, like a boat beached above the waterline.

clue.text: Very busy in that arid resort

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort says the letters of that and arid are sorted again

explanation.surface: Tourism staff are rushed off their feet at a desert holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but is read as re-sort, an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hard at it is an idiom for working energetically and without pause.

clue.text: Black chest in study

indicators.note: in says the chest piece goes inside the study piece

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A dark box sits in someone's office.
explanation.definitionFit: To black something is to darken it, making it black or dim.
